findings.text: the resume writer's session_resumed: True has no test that would fail if the line were dropped; the only test reaching it (tests/test_crew.py resume path) is not-run in the gate cohort and never asserted the key, so the third writer of the pair is exercised by nothing.

a delegated in-harness launch records session_resumed: False although reckon never launched a command to resume; "this run did not resume" and "reckon cannot put a label on this launch" are different facts sharing one false, which is a weaker version of the conflation the node removed (the comment above the line says so, so it is documented rather than hidden).

a pointer written before the rename and then resumed carries session_resumed without session_reuse_capable, because record_resumption writes only the act key while the capability comes from the record's own history; the manifest's "all three writers carry the pair" is therefore imprecise, and a reader treating an absent capability key as false would read a legacy record as a run that could not have resumed, which is not what the absence means.

justifications.durability: the pair holds, but its third writer is unguarded — record_resumption (dispatch.py:4497) sets session_resumed with no test that fails if the line is dropped, because the only test reaching that path (tests/test_crew.py) is not-run in the prescribed cohort (probe exit 124 at base and head alike) and never asserted session_resumed even when it ran.
justifications.evidence: the falsifier is the right shape and I reproduced it myself rather than reading the worker's logs — the new file fails 5/5 at base 09615744 with a uniform KeyError: 'session_reuse_capable' and passes 5/5 at head 1f250057 (/tmp/rev-run-record-3283259/my_base.log, my_head.log), and I re-measured the population (41 live pointers, 41 carrying the old key true, 37 of those with no session_id) instead of quoting the brief's 51/45.
justifications.fit: the two names read as act versus capability and the new tests assert the old key's absence from the record ("session_reuse" not in dispatched / moved, tests/test_run_record_reports_actual_resume.py), so no reader of a fresh record can keep taking the lane's setting for an observation.
justifications.goal_fidelity: dispatch.py:3180,3267,4381,4497 split the always-true capability copy into session_reuse_capable (the lane's setting) and session_resumed (this run's act), derived by _launched_prior_session (dispatch.py:3469) from plan.resumed_session required to appear as an argv token — the run's own launch, not the config it launched under.
justifications.scope_discipline: both commits touch only the four declared paths (git show --stat 1f250057 505f34cc) and the reviewed worktree is clean at 505f34cc, with the plan section and evidence anchor landing inside the fence rather than around it.
